summary.plain_language_summary: Your heart testing found a faster-than-usual rhythm, but no sustained abnormal rhythm or structural heart problem was seen. Your blood count and iron tests show low iron and anemia, which may be relevant to your tiredness, reduced exercise tolerance, lightheadedness, and difficulty concentrating, although the records do not prove one cause. The positive stool blood test and the stomach erosions and ulcer make it important to complete the recommended digestive-system follow-up. Your endoscopy report also says to avoid ibuprofen and similar medicines, while you report using ibuprofen most days; please discuss this promptly with your doctors. Your TSH was mildly high with a normal free T4, so follow-up testing and discussion are appropriate rather than drawing a conclusion from this result alone. The stomach biopsy results are still pending, and heavier periods are also worth reviewing in the context of the low iron.

key_findings.text: The blood count shows low hemoglobin and small red blood cells, while iron studies show low iron stores and low circulating iron. This is relevant to discuss alongside fatigue and reduced exercise tolerance.
The stool test was positive for blood, and a colonoscopy was recommended but had not yet been scheduled in the report.
Endoscopy showed stomach erosions and a small ulcer without active bleeding during the procedure. The report notes ibuprofen use and H. pylori as possible contributors.
The H. pylori stool test was positive, and stomach biopsy results were pending in the endoscopy report.
Heart monitoring showed a faster-than-usual rate but no sustained abnormal rhythm; the heart ultrasound showed normal pumping and no significant valve problem.
TSH was slightly above the report's range while free T4 was within range; the specialist recommends follow-up rather than concluding that thyroid function explains the symptoms.
The platelet count was mildly above the report's range and was noted as something to recheck alongside the blood count and iron follow-up.
You report heavier periods, near-daily headaches, frequent ibuprofen use, ice craving, and difficulty concentrating; these symptoms are relevant context for discussions with your clinicians.

connections.text: Low iron and anemia may help explain some of the fatigue, reduced exercise tolerance, concentration difficulty, and faster heart rate, but the records do not establish a single cause.

The positive stool blood test, low iron, and stomach findings make completing the recommended digestive-system evaluation important; the stomach findings do not establish the source of the positive stool test.

Frequent ibuprofen use connects the near-daily headache concern with the endoscopy advice to avoid NSAIDs and the stomach ulcer and erosions. Review the reported amount and frequency with the treating clinicians.
Heavier periods may be relevant to discussing iron loss alongside the low iron results and the positive stool blood test; the records do not establish the source of the iron deficiency.
The mildly high TSH with normal free T4 is worth following up, but the available result does not show that thyroid function is the cause of the cold feeling, hair shedding, or other symptoms.

The heart evaluation is reassuring about structure and sustained rhythm problems, while the faster sinus rate and exertional symptoms still merit review alongside blood counts, iron, and other possible contributors.

Patient: Dana Whitfield    DOB: 03/12/1984    Date of visit: 07/29/2026
Consultant: Anika Rhodes, MD (Cardiology)

HISTORY
42-year-old woman with 4 months of palpitations, worse climbing stairs,
with fatigue and occasional lightheadedness on standing. No chest pain,
no fainting. Drinks 2 cups of coffee a day. No prior heart history.

VITAL SIGNS
BP 108/68   HR 102 (regular)   SpO2 99% on room air   BMI 23.1

Regular rhythm, mildly fast. Soft 2/6 systolic flow murmur at the left
sternal border. Lungs clear. No leg swelling.

- ECG today: sinus tachycardia, otherwise normal (separate report).
- 48-hour Holter (07/15-07/17/2026): sinus rhythm throughout. Average HR
  96, maximum 148 with exertion, minimum 68 asleep. Rare isolated PACs
  (<1% of beats). No atrial fibrillation, no sustained arrhythmia.
- Echocardiogram (07/22/2026): normal left ventricular size and function,
  ejection fraction 60%. No significant valve disease. Murmur consistent
  with a benign flow murmur.
- Recent blood counts were not available at the time of this visit.

ASSESSMENT
Palpitations with sinus tachycardia and a structurally normal heart.
No arrhythmia identified.

PLAN
1. Propranolol 10 mg by mouth up to twice daily as needed for palpitations.
2. Reduce caffeine.
3. Return in 6 months, sooner if fainting or chest pain.

LAKESIDE DIGESTIVE HEALTH - UPPER ENDOSCOPY (EGD) REPORT
Patient: Dana Whitfield        DOB: 03/12/1984
Date of procedure: 09/02/2026  Endoscopist: Marcus Feld, MD

INDICATIONS
Iron-deficiency anemia, positive fecal immunochemical test, 3 months of
upper abdominal discomfort and bloating, daily ibuprofen use for
headaches, positive H. pylori stool antigen.

FINDINGS
Esophagus: normal.
Stomach: patchy redness of the antrum with 5 to 6 small superficial
erosions. One 6 mm clean-based ulcer in the antrum with no active
bleeding and no visible vessel.
Duodenum: normal to the second portion.

BIOPSIES
Gastric antrum and body (H. pylori, histology). Ulcer margin sampled per
standard practice. Duodenal biopsies to exclude celiac disease.
Pathology: PENDING at the time of this report.

IMPRESSION
Antral erosions and a small clean-based gastric ulcer, most likely
related to NSAID use and/or H. pylori infection.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Avoid ibuprofen and other NSAIDs.
2. Omeprazole 40 mg daily before breakfast for 8 weeks.
3. Treat H. pylori once pathology is back.
4. Colonoscopy recommended to complete the evaluation of iron deficiency
   and the positive FIT (not yet scheduled).
5. Clinic follow-up to review pathology in 2 to 3 weeks.
